fact: The bright eye of the Crane, a hot blue star of the deep south.
bio: Alnair (Alpha Gruis) is a hot blue-white star about 101 light-years away, the brightest in the modern constellation Grus, the Crane. It shines with a clean blue-white light in the southern sky.
cultural: Its name comes from an Arabic phrase, 'the bright one', inherited from an older constellation figure. Grus was formed by late-16th-century navigators charting the southern stars.
